column1: # Reference sequences for the marker-gene PHYLOGENIES (code/analysis/17..19).
# These are NOT the search probes in metadata/target_markers.tsv. Those exist
# only so blastn/tblastn can find a locus inside a contig. THESE are the named
# species that go into the tree next to your samples and give a tip its
# identity -- type strains, described endosymbionts, and the published
# tick-derived sequences the Australian literature is built on.
# Every query runs against nuccore and returns NUCLEOTIDE records, because the
# trees are built on nucleotides. A record does not have to be a clean gene
# record: step 18 blasts each one and cuts out the marker locus, so a whole
# genome is a perfectly good source (see metadata/tree_ref_genomes.tsv, which
# supplies genomes for every locus of a target).
# Step 18 then throws away anything that does not actually carry the locus at
# the panel's min_pident / min_aln_len, so a loose query costs download time,
#   target         must match a `target` in metadata/target_markers.tsv
#   n_refs         how many records to KEEP from this query (after the
#   query          Entrez nuccore term; ' ||| ' separates fallbacks, tried in
#   outgroup_n     how many outgroup records to keep (0 = none; the tree is
#   outgroup_query Entrez term for the outgroup, same rules
# A target x marker with sample sequences but NO row here still gets a tree:
# step 17 falls back to an auto-generated query and marks it `auto` in the
# manifest. Add a row here to do better than the guess.

column4: query
column6: outgroup_query
